physics_goals.quote: HADES is a versatile magnetic spectrometer aimed at studying dielectron production in pion, proton and heavy-ion induced collisions.
physics_goals.value: Study dielectron production in pion, proton and heavy-ion induced collisions: hadron properties in nuclei and in hot, dense hadronic matter

summary.plain: HADES is a magnetic spectrometer at GSI in Darmstadt that records electron-positron pairs and hadrons from proton, pion and heavy-ion collisions at about 1 to 2 GeV per nucleon. It probes the hot, dense, baryon-rich matter found in neutron-star mergers. It has run since before 2004.
summary.technical: High-Acceptance DiElectron Spectrometer: six superconducting-coil toroidal magnet, hadron-blind RICH, drift chambers, time of flight and a multiplicity/electron trigger (85% azimuthal coverage, 18-85 degrees polar), at the SIS18 for dielectron and strangeness studies in p, pi and heavy-ion (C+C, Ar+KCl, Au+Au, Ag+Ag) collisions; Au+Au at 1.23 AGeV (sqrt(sNN) = 2.4 GeV) gave the fireball temperature of about 72 MeV.
